name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd.
business_summary: India's dominant commodity derivatives exchange (about 98% share of listed commodity futures/options): bullion (gold, silver), energy (crude oil, natural gas) and base metals contracts, regulated by SEBI. Revenue comes from transaction fees on futures and options turnover. Q2 FY27 revenue ~Rs 800 cr (+114% y/y), PAT Rs 455 cr (+130%); operating margin 76%; stock +81% over 12m and +50% in 2026 but fell 5-7% on 4 Nov despite results. It is investing Rs 200 cr in coal and minerals platforms and has near-zero debt.

cost_structure.note: technology and clearing costs; opex Rs 189 cr Q2 on Rs 800 cr sales

exposures.mechanism: Bullion (gold/silver) futures and options are the largest revenue lines (model knowledge ~40-50%). Revenue ~ notional turnover x fee. Gold +8% -> notional +8% on ~25% of revenue = +2% revenue; EBITDA margin 74-76% -> EBITDA +2.7%; EV/MCap 0.97; persistence 0.4 -> +1.0; volatility effect (gold -8.4% since June, silver -30%) raises option activity -> +1.5. Wide because volumes depend on volatility not level.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 revenue ~Rs 800 cr (+114%), PAT Rs 455 cr (+130%) (Economic Times)

exposures.mechanism: Silver +12%: silver is the highest-turnover metal in retail options; +12% notional on ~20% of revenue = +2.4% -> EBITDA +3.2% x 0.4 persistence = +1.3; crash in silver (-30% since Jun) coincided with record volume => sign of price effect ambiguous; +1.5, wide.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 revenue ~Rs 800 cr (+114%), PAT Rs 455 cr (+130%) (Economic Times)

exposures.mechanism: Crude oil futures/options are the second-largest revenue line (~30%, model knowledge). +10% Brent -> notional +10% x 30% = +3% revenue -> EBITDA +4% x 0.4 = +1.6; empirical +1.32/SSU (t 1.8) agrees -> +1.3.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27 revenue ~Rs 800 cr (+114%), PAT Rs 455 cr (+130%) (Economic Times)

exposures.mechanism: Natural gas options are a smaller line (~5% of revenue); +15% price -> +0.7% revenue -> +0.3 equity; empirical -0.66 (t -1.2) not significant.
Base metals (copper, aluminium, zinc) ~8% of revenue; +10% -> +0.8% revenue; empirical aluminium +2.60/SSU (t 2.2) reflects commodity-volatility co-movement, shrunk to +0.3.

Retail F&O/commodity participation is correlated; +20% traded value/demat additions -> +8% MCX options turnover -> +5% revenue -> EBITDA +6.5% x 0.5 = +3.2; empirical US equities +2.88 (t 2.7) supports risk-on link; +3.

One tightening step (weekly-expiry curbs, lot-size increase, margin/position limits, higher CTT or option premium charges) cut options volumes 20-40% in equity (model knowledge on 2024-25 episode); on MCX options ~60% of revenue -> -15% revenue -> EBITDA -20% x 0.5 persistence x EV/MCap 0.97 -> -9.7, probability-weighted for 'a step' -> -5, range -12..-1.

evidence.note: Bernstein prefers MCX over BSE as equity-derivative volumes fell (ET)

exposures.mechanism: Entry/scale-up of BSE or NSE in commodity derivatives (BSE re-entered 2025, NSE application - model knowledge, verify). 10% share loss in bullion/crude options -> -10% revenue... assuming 25% at risk -> -7% EBITDA x 0.6 x 0.97 -> -4; rounded -3.
Household/institutional hedging and trading in commodities (gold ETF-spot linkage, MSME hedging) widens; MCX market share ~98% in listed commodity derivatives; revenue grew 128% TTM; +1 SSU -> +2.

Rupee-denominated bullion/crude contracts rise with INR depreciation (gold INR price = USD price x USD/INR): +3% -> +3% notional on ~70% of revenue = +2% revenue -> EBITDA +2.7% x 0.4 = +1.1; empirical +3.83 (t 1.9) larger -> +1.2.
Volatility spikes lift hedging demand but cut retail participation; empirical -0.79 (t -1.3); net small negative -0.5.
FIIs 27.06% (swinging 26-30% in 2026) - ownership by foreign exchange-theme funds; +1.5 beyond beta.
Minor; relevant only if bank participation (members) is curbed.
